assignment: Computational inference: latent-variable EM, variational inference/ELBO, Laplace and integration, ABC/simulation-based inference, identifiability/approximation bias. Generic factorization and optimization prerequisites must be in Category 3 or earlier; no Category 4 dependency.
extraction: PDF text extracted page-by-page with PyMuPDF 1.27.2.3; page counts below are physical PDF pages. HTML sources were retained and converted to text with Python standard-library HTMLParser. Hashes are SHA256 of exact raw source and local extracted text bytes. Extraction is not itself evidence of reading; each read range/status is separately recorded.

sources.title: Lecture Notes on the EM Algorithm
sources.publication: Author lecture notes, Instituto de Telecomunicações / Instituto Superior Técnico
sources.read_status: Relevant tutorial complete: PDF pp.1-7 (printed pp.1-7), §§1-4. Read incomplete/complete data setup, E/M definitions, auxiliary-function/KL monotonicity, GEM Q-ascent, fixed-point/stationarity discussion, and exponential-family update.
sources.claims_and_hypotheses: Ascent is for valid likelihoods and conditional latent distributions with defined expectations; exact M-step maximizes Q, GEM increases Q. The auxiliary identity establishes monotonicity only.
sources.limitations: The note's statement that zero KL forces parameter equality is false without parameter identifiability (conditional laws can coincide at different parameter values). Its exposition does not prove general convergence of the EM sequence; no such result is imported.

sources.title: Convex Optimization
sources.read_status: Relevant units complete: PDF pp.477-483 and 498-505; corresponding printed Chapter 9 §§9.2-9.3, pp.463-469, and §9.5, pp.484-491.
anchors: strong-convexity/smoothness gradient bounds on a sublevel set
§9.5 damped Newton, Hessian-Lipschitz error bound, line search, local quadratic phase
sources.claims_and_hypotheses: Gradient rates require the stated positive lower and finite upper Hessian bounds on the relevant sublevel set and the specified step rule. Newton local rates require nonsingular positive curvature and local Hessian regularity; damping/globalization conditions are separate.
sources.limitations: These results do not establish global optimization of nonconvex statistical objectives or posterior unimodality. Exact coordinate-ascent nondecrease is proved directly in the planned VI pair.

sources.title: Variational Inference: A Review for Statisticians
sources.authors: David M. Blei, Alp Kucukelbir, and Jon D. McAuliffe
sources.publication: Journal of the American Statistical Association 112(518), 859-877; arXiv:1601.00670
sources.read_status: Relevant exposition complete: PDF pp.1-11, full §1 and §2.1-2.5. Remaining paper not used for this assignment.
anchors: coordinate-ascent update q_j proportional to exp(E_{-j} log joint)
local optima, Gaussian covariance underestimation, log-sum-exp/numerical notes
sources.claims_and_hypotheses: The ELBO identity assumes a proper posterior and meaningful finite log expectations; coordinate maximization requires a well-defined normalizer and an attained exact optimum.
sources.limitations: Review-level derivations, not generic global convergence/calibration theorems. Its discussion expressly warns that reverse-KL mean-field can miss dependence and underestimate variance.

sources.title: An Introduction to Variational Methods for Graphical Models
sources.authors: Michael I. Jordan, Zoubin Ghahramani, Tommi Jaakkola, and Lawrence K. Saul
sources.read_status: Relevant independent derivation complete: PDF pp.31-38, printed pp.213-220, §§6.1-6.3.
anchors: finite/discrete KL and Jensen evidence bound
EM as coordinate ascent in ELBO
sources.claims_and_hypotheses: Discrete finite-state calculations assume normalizable distributions and finite sums; continuous generalization requires measure/integrability hypotheses stated in BCS.
sources.limitations: No graphical-model or neural-network item is imported. The source supplies a second derivation, not a generic accuracy or convergence guarantee.

sources.limitations: It refers detailed proof/error bounds to Olver/Boyd/Wong; no full proof or remainder bound is claimed read here. The local multivariate interior theorem still requires a Cat3 proof.

sources.title: Fundamentals and Recent Developments in Approximate Bayesian Computation
sources.authors: Jarno Lintusaari, Michael U. Gutmann, Ritabrata Dutta, Samuel Kaski, and Jukka Corander
sources.read_status: Selected units read: PDF pp.1-6, 10-23, 46-47. Physical PDF has 47 pages; pp.24-45 not read.
anchors: intro/simulator model and rejection ABC target, pp.1-6, 10-13
MCMC-ABC target and acceptance ratio, pp.19-23
MCMC-ABC and SMC-ABC algorithms, appendix pp.46-47
sources.claims_and_hypotheses: ABC induces a summary/tolerance target; summary reduction and tolerance introduce distinct approximation sources. ABC-MCMC/SMC algorithms require their own transition/resampling assumptions.
sources.limitations: Review/tutorial source; its cited asymptotic bandwidth rates are not proved here. Application/method pages 24-45 not used. Do not conflate exact ABC algorithm targeting its approximate law with exact full-data Bayes.

sources.title: Constructing Summary Statistics for Approximate Bayesian Computation: Semi-automatic ABC
sources.publication: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society: Series B 74(3), 419-474; arXiv:1004.1112
sources.read_status: Selected units and main proofs read: PDF pp.1-18 (intro, kernels/noisy ABC, Theorems 1-4) and pp.35-38 (Appendix A variance comments, Appendix B full proof of Lemma 1, Appendix C proof of Theorem 4). Pages 19-34 and 39-44 not read.
anchors: kernel ABC targets and calibration/noisy ABC
Theorem 3: posterior mean is optimal summary for the stated squared-error loss
Lemma 1 acceptance order and explicit smoothness/support assumptions
sources.claims_and_hypotheses: The posterior-mean summary result is loss-specific; asymptotic acceptance statements use the article's explicit local smoothness/support conditions. Calibration is under prior-predictive repetition and the noise-augmented observation model.
sources.limitations: Do not turn calibration into fixed-parameter frequentist coverage. Application pages not read; no universal tolerance rate or coverage guarantee claimed.

sources.read_status: Algorithmic pages read: PDF pp.1-6, printed pp.2025-2030. Remaining example pages not relied upon.
sources.claims_and_hypotheses: Regression adjustment is a local approximation around accepted summaries and depends on support/tolerance and regression fit; it is not exact Bayes at nonzero tolerance.
sources.limitations: The worked population-genetics application is not used to establish a general theorem.
